description: Operator-valued A^λ_{μν}(I) extraction via bilinear-system inversion. Confirms refined Sub-lemma 2.1: the (μ,ν)-block of ρ_λ(I) is generally a non-scalar operator on V_μ ⊗ V_ν. For the deuteron interface I = σ_2 - h(1/2 - δ/4) on H_6 ↓ H_3 × H_3 — the canonical COLOUR-WEIGHTED p-n crossing, ctype `averaged_weighted` — all 11 λ admit consistent operator-valued A^λ_{μν} solutions to machine precision; only the 1-dim extreme λ ∈ {(6), (1^6)} have scalar A^λ_{μν}. The extracted matrices are the concrete categorical inputs the Hoefsmit-formula derivation must reproduce per docs/audits/2026-05-04-sublemma-2-1-categorical-proof.md.

parameters.interface: I = σ_2 - h(1/2 - δ/4)  [ctype `averaged_weighted`: the canonical colour-weighted p-n crossing]

precision.accuracy_ceiling_cause: Set by the 50-digit q_0 literal (q_parameter.Q_50_DIGIT_STR) and the working precision, NOT by the rep. char_fast now builds the seminormal rep symbolically in q (PR #5517, bean qou-v6vp), so the input data is no longer float64: perturbing q_0 at the k-th digit moves this producer's matrices by ~2e-k, measured to k=60, where before the same test moved them by exactly 0.0. This is INTERNAL consistency at the given q_0 literal; the physical q_0 is pinned by a CODATA ratio and is known to nothing like 50 digits.
precision.accuracy_ceiling_history: This field read '~1e-16' until PR #5517, caused by _cached_seminormal substituting q at build time and returning float64. That is fixed; the residuals below moved from ~1e-15 to ~1e-70 for every rank>1 lambda as a result, while the two rank-1 lambdas (scalar action, no rep matrix) did not move.
